children: Cash remittances coursed through banks in the Philippines grew by 1.9% year-on-year to USD 3.18 billion in July 2026, up from USD 3.17 billion a year earlier.
This marked the highest level of monthly inflow since December last year.
The US remained the largest source of remittances, accounting for 39.7% of total inflows, followed by Singapore (7.1%), Saudi Arabia (6.3%), Japan (5.0%), and the UK (4.7%).
In the first seven months of the year, cash remittances rose by 2.3% to USD 20.39 billion from USD 19.93 in the corresponding period a year earlier.

Meanwhile, personal remittances, which include transfers through banks, informal channels, and in-kind transfers, increased by 2.0% to USD 3.60 billion in July and grew by 2.3% to USD 22.73 billion on a year-to-date basis.

title: Philippine Cash Remittances Rise 1.9% in July
